title: Polly resilience (retry, circuit breaker, timeout)
hook: Polly adds resilience policies to HTTP clients and service calls — retry transient failures, open a circuit breaker when downstream is unhealthy, and enforce timeouts so slow dependencies do not stall your entire API.

blocks.text: Polly is a .NET resilience library integrated with IHttpClientFactory via Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience (.NET 8+) and Polly v8 pipelines. Policies compose as retry, circuit breaker, timeout, hedging, and bulkhead. HttpClient named clients attach AddStandardResilienceHandler() or custom Polly pipelines. Circuit breaker stops calling a failing dependency for a cooling period — fail fast instead of queueing thread-pool work on timeouts. Retry must be idempotent or limited to safe verbs and known transient status codes.

entries.plainDefinition: Re-executes failed operations with backoff for transient errors (503, timeout, socket reset).
After failure threshold, rejects calls immediately until half-open probe succeeds.
Cancels operation exceeding deadline — prevents unbounded waits.
Trial period after break — one success closes circuit; failure reopens.
entries.example: Single probe request allowed through breaker

blocks.text: APIs calling payment, inventory, or identity services need controlled failure modes. Naive retry on POST doubles charges. Missing circuit breaker during outage causes retry storms that starve the thread pool — every request waits for timeout. Polly plus HttpClientFactory avoids socket exhaustion by reusing handlers while policies wrap each call.

blocks.title: Retry only idempotent operations
blocks.body: Safe: GET, HEAD, PUT with idempotency key. Dangerous: POST payment without idempotency — use circuit breaker and timeout without blind retry, or retry only on 408/429 with idempotency header.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Closed (normal)
items.body: Calls pass through; failures increment counter.

items.title: Threshold exceeded
items.body: Breaker opens — immediate BrokenCircuitException without calling downstream.

items.title: Open (fail fast)
items.body: API returns 503 or fallback; downstream recovers without load.

items.title: Half-open
items.body: After break duration, one trial call permitted.

items.title: Closed again
items.body: Trial success resets failure count; failure reopens circuit.

diagram.title: Polly pipeline on HttpClient

stateDiagram-v2

snippet.label: .NET 8 standard resilience handler on HttpClient
snippet.explanation: AddStandardResilienceHandler bundles retry, circuit breaker, attempt timeout, and total timeout. Set HttpClient.Timeout infinite so Polly controls deadlines consistently.

snippet.label: Polly v8 custom pipeline — retry + circuit breaker
snippet.explanation: ShouldHandle limits retry/breaker to 5xx and network errors — not 404. MinimumThroughput avoids opening breaker on first failure in low traffic.

snippet.label: Map BrokenCircuitException to Problem Details
snippet.explanation: Clients distinguish breaker open (503 + retryAfter) from business not-found (404). Do not retry 503 from breaker with same storm intensity — honor backoff.

snippet.label: Failure-mode diagnostic — log breaker state transitions
snippet.explanation: Alert on OnOpened — correlates with downstream outage or latency SLO breach. Pair with dependency metrics in Application Insights.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Retry on all exceptions including 400 Bad Request. HttpClient.Timeout shorter than Polly total timeout (double cancel race). No jitter on retry (thundering herd on recovery). Circuit breaker per instance without shared state — each pod opens independently (often acceptable).

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: Application Insights dependency failures drop when breaker opens — latency p95 may improve (fail fast). Log OnOpened events aligned with downstream incident. dotnet-trace shows threads blocked in HttpClient.SendAsync when timeout policy missing. Interview scenario: payment API — retry GET balance, breaker on inventory, never retry POST capture without idempotency key.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Retrying POST payments blindly. Cannot draw circuit breaker states. Saying Polly replaces need for rate limiting. Ignoring HttpClientFactory — new HttpClient per request exhausts ports.

interviewTakeaways: Polly composes retry, circuit breaker, timeout, and bulkhead on HttpClient via IHttpClientFactory.
When not to use retry: non-idempotent POST without idempotency key; breaker without minimum throughput tuning.
Production tip: AddStandardResilienceHandler defaults; log OnOpened; map BrokenCircuitException to 503 with retryAfter.

60s: Retry handles transient 5xx with backoff. Breaker opens after failure ratio — fail fast, half-open probe, close on success. Timeout cancels hung calls. HttpClientFactory plus Polly avoids socket exhaustion.
Follow-up: difference between attempt timeout and total request timeout in standard handler?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'retry three times on any error' gets you rejected — 400 and 404 are not transient; POST may duplicate side effects.
Creating new HttpClient() in a loop — SNAT port exhaustion despite Polly.
Strong answer: 'Standard resilience on GET clients; breaker opens at 50% failures with min throughput 20; payment POST uses timeout and breaker only, idempotency key for safe retry.'
